dog.description_text:
This pet needs emergency placement. Please click here to go to our emergency placement page for more information.

This pet is available only through ACC New Hope partners. To adopt or foster, please complete the pre-screener form below. Inquiries sent directly to ACC will not receive a response.

Pre-Screener Form

Will is at risk due to behavioral concerns. Will was brought to the Care Centers alongside another dog. Upon evaluation, both dogs were found to have multiple puncture wounds reportedly sustained during an altercation with each other. During his time in the Care Centers, Will has displayed inconsistent behavior toward staff, at times lunging at certain individuals while also demonstrating social behavior with staff and volunteers. On walks, he has attempted to chase birds and small animals and has occasionally displayed a tense posture around other dogs. Sometimes, Will becomes over stimulated on walks and will repeatedly jump on staff. Although Will's behavior has fluctuated throughout his stay, he continues to engage socially with staff and volunteers. He participated in trainings and gets excited about enrichment. Medically, Will is apparently healthy.

Will came into ACC as a stray. Because of this we do not know how he would be in a home environment. Will was brought to the Care Centers alongside another dog. Upon evaluation, both dogs were found to have multiple puncture wounds reportedly sustained during an altercation with each other. During his time in the Care Centers, Will has displayed inconsistent behavior toward staff, at times lunging at certain individuals while also demonstrating social behavior with staff and volunteers. Will is noted to be highly dog reactive and at times difficult to redirect. On walks, he has been noted to attempt to chase birds and small animals. Will is noted to be a volunteer favorite. We recommend placement with a New Hope partner who can provide any necessary behavior modification (force-free, positive reinforcement-based) and re-evaluate his behavior in a stable home environment before placement into a permanent home.
